newsitem.title: UK: European bars experience falling beer sales - survey.
newsitem.headline: European bars experience falling beer sales - survey.

text.p: European bars, the leading outlets for beer sales, have been the worst hit by growing consumer awareness of the dangers of alcohol consumption as well as from recession, said a survey by Datamonitor.
"In Eire, although volume sales of beer are not falling, bars and pubs are increasingly losing market share due to diversifying social tastes," said the survey.
"As restaurants and alternative leisure activities develop, Irish pubs are entering a decline which will continue into the next century."
Similarly in France and Germany, bar sales are suffering because the ageing population increasingly prefers to go out to restaurants, said the report.
In Denmark and Spain, however, beer sales through bars are set to increase as a result of the market recovering from recession, said the survey.

In other countries, bars are holding onto their share by changing their look -- in Sweden for instance bar operators are profiting from industry deregulation by hosting local functions and festivities, said the survey.
In Britain, pubs have improved the standard of food available and developed theme pubs.
